# pacman.conf fixtures

Configuration files and the output the real tools gave for them. The tests in
`conf_fixture_test.go` parse every top-level `*.conf` here and compare the
result with `expected/`, option by option and repository by repository.

## Provenance

`expected/` is generated by `generate.sh` on an x86_64 Arch Linux host with the
tools that ship with pacman:

| File | Content |
| --- | --- |
| `expected/<name>.txt` | `pacman-conf -c <name>.conf`: every option and repository as pacman resolved it |
| `expected/<name>.warn` | the same run's stderr: the "directive ... not recognized" warnings |
| `expected/<name>.repos` | `pacman-conf -c <name>.conf --repo-list` |
| `expected/invalid/<name>.err` | stderr of the run on `invalid/<name>.conf`, which pacman-conf rejects |
| `expected/VERSION` | `pacman-conf --version`, the pacman/libalpm version and `uname -m` |

The committed outputs come from pacman 7.1.0 with libalpm 16.0.1 on x86_64
(see `expected/VERSION`).

## Regenerating

```sh
./generate.sh
```

The script runs from this directory, because the fixtures include each other
with relative paths. The host needs `pacman-conf` and `pacman`; `RootDir`,
`DBPath` and `GPGDir` must name directories that exist (the fixtures use
`/usr`, `/usr/lib` and `/usr/bin`), and `Architecture = auto` resolves to the
host's `uname -m`. The tests render that as `x86_64`, so regenerate on x86_64.

## Layout

- `full.conf` uses every option and the repository keys, with includes.
- `defaults.conf`, `rootdir.conf`, `lists.conf`, `arch_auto.conf`,
  `usage.conf`, `unknown.conf` and `sections.conf` cover defaults, the
  root-relative paths, repeated list and single-value options, `Usage`,
  unknown directives and section naming.
- `siglevel_*.conf` cover SigLevel inheritance between the global level,
  `LocalFileSigLevel`, `RemoteFileSigLevel` and each repository.
- `mirrors/`, `conf.d/`, `glob_order.conf` and `depth10.conf` exercise
  `Include`: globs, nesting, a section opened inside an included file, and the
  deepest chain pacman accepts (`chain/`: ten levels).
- `invalid/` holds files pacman-conf rejects: bad values, a directive outside
  a section, a missing include or glob match, an include loop and an eleventh
  nesting level (`chain/c1.conf` starts a chain of eleven).
